Hi Ash —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from my side and the open items we agreed to own: 

1) Latency targets: CoreHealth reiterated 99th percentile <= 200ms for interactive screening flows (avg token length ~60) and <= 350ms for long-form clinical summaries (avg token length ~450).
2) Concurrency/throughput: expected bursty traffic at end of business hours: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions and baseline 30 qps.
3) Streaming: low-latency token streaming is required (clients consume partial hypotheses).
4) Regional routing & data residency: EU patient data must remain in eu-central for EU users; APAC traffic should prefer ap-southeast but can failover to us-west if we log residency fallback and encrypt in transit per their legal team.

Attached I dropped the SLO template (slo_requirements.xlsx) and the recording from today. Next steps:
- Rishi: can you confirm whether we can meet 200ms p99 for the short-flow with our current Kestrel quant profile and what concurrency headroom looks like?
- David: can you draft a reserved capacity estimate and outline what Dedicated pools + burst would cost for the initial 6-month pilot?
- Ash: please confirm whether the APAC fallback to us-west is acceptable subject to audit logging and encryption, or whether you need on-prem evaluation.

Thanks — aiming to get a technical note back by EOD Wednesday so we can feed Procurement.

Best,

Kimberly / Ash —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick technical responses (high-level):

- Latency (short-flow, ~60 tokens): with the Kestrel v2 quantized runtime and continuous batching tuned to 8ms batch latency, we expect p50 ~30–40ms, p95 ~120–150ms, p99 in the 170–230ms range depending on network tail. Meeting p99 <=200ms is achievable in us-west and eu-central under reserved capacity with the following caveats:
  * Need dedicated concurrency headroom: reserve ~250 concurrent model slots (each slot ~80ms GPU time per token stream for short flows) to handle peak bursts without significant batching delay.
  * For APAC, model serving in ap-southeast gives similar numbers but network RTT adds ~60–90ms to p99; to hit 200ms p99 in APAC we will need local serving in ap-southeast and optimized kernel (FP16 + int8 fallback).

- Long-form summaries (avg 450 tokens, streaming): token-by-token streaming increases compute; expect p99 ~320–400ms in us/eu on dedicated nodes with recommended batching window tuned to 20ms. Achieving <=350ms p99 requires tighter autoscaling and a higher GPU worker density to avoid queuing.

- Throughput/Concurrency: baseline 30 qps + 200 concurrent streaming sessions maps to ~18k tokens per minute sustained during peak windows; this looks like ~6–8 A100-equivalent worker nodes (depending on quant levels). Exact #s in the attached estimator.

- Routing & residency: we can bind EU user traffic to eu-central and APAC to ap-southeast via smart routing policies. For APAC fallback to us-west we will mark requests as "residency-fallback" in logs and provide signed export of those logs for audits. If CoreHealth requires zero-fallback, we should discuss a private deployment option in APAC or an on-prem proxy.

I'll compile a short tech note with SLA tradeoffs and two capacity options (pilot vs production) and drop it to the thread by Wednesday EOD.

—Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ash Patel <ash@corehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & geo-routing constraints for CoreHealth pilot

Thanks Kim / Rishi — appreciate the rapid follow-up. A couple clarifications from Legal & Engineering after reviewing the recording and SLO sheet: 

1) EU residents: zero-fallback is preferred but Legal will accept fallback to a geo-isolated us-west region if we can: a) provide quarterly attestations that no patient data persists outside eu-central, b) provide searchable, signed logs when fallback occurs, and c) encrypt session-level blobs with customer-managed KMS keys.

2) APAC: they prefer local ap-southeast serving for latency reasons; fallback to us-west is acceptable only if (a) we preserve residency metadata and (b) Redwood provides a runbook for audit.

3) Commercial: Procurement asked for a 6-month pilot quote (including Dedicated buffer for peak) and a TCO example if we move to private deployment in APAC.

I'll loop in Procurement separately but please prioritize the pilot sizing and a short one-page note summarizing residency guarantees we can commit to for pilot.

Ash
